clinician.trajectory_summary: A baby girl was born at term with a post-auricular swelling noted soon after delivery that gradually enlarged with pus-like discharge. Prenatal ultrasound identified a cystic mass in the right post-auricular area. At 15 days of age, physical examination showed a large (12x18 cm), lobulated mass cystic superiorly and firm inferiorly, non-tender, mobile with hyperpigmented overlying skin and no systemic signs. Laboratory work revealed neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated CRP, and very high alpha-fetoprotein (7390.5 ng/L). Cranial ultrasound detected Arnold–Chiari malformation grade 1 and echocardiography moderate atrial septal defect. Histopathology of a biopsy specimen demonstrated mature tissue elements including cuboidal epithelium-lined cysts, epithelial glands, respiratory epithelium with mucus cells, mature adipose tissue, nerve tissue, and blood vessels, consistent with a mature cystic teratoma. Brain MRI and CT angiography at 30 days showed a mixed type teratoma with erosion of parietal and temporal bones. No documented surgical intervention or clinical outcome was reported.
